results.reason: Issue 1 states the DA §3.2 Renewal Notice deadline was about Aug. 16, 2026 and that no notice appears to have been delivered. It says the DA expires Nov. 14, 2026, before the Nov. 30 closing. It also says the MIPA §3.12(c) 'through November 2029' rep and the Schedule 3.12 note are inaccurate, with indemnity and closing exposure for the Sellers.

Issue 2 treats the 100% sale as a Change of Control under DA §1.3/§14.2 that requires prior written consent, with an immediate termination right under §14.3/§15.4. It notes the consent is missing from Sched. 3.6, so the §6.4 covenant and §7.1(d) condition do not cover it. It recommends requesting the consent now and adding it to Sched. 3.6.

Issue 4 notes SL §1.1 adds NY and VA, and cites DA §19.4 to show the SL ranks above the DA body. It explains the non-compete and 18-month tail cover six states while exclusivity covers only four. It recommends conforming the territory or extending exclusivity.

Issue 6 contrasts SL §6.1–6.2 (New York law, New York County forum) with DA §18.1–18.2 (Delaware law, Wilmington courts). It explains a single dispute could be split across two forums and two laws, and recommends conforming the SL to Delaware law and forum.
The memo states the Initial Term ends Nov. 14, 2026 (DA §3.1) and references the DA dated Nov. 15, 2023.
The memo states the target closing is Nov. 30, 2026 (MIPA §2.2).
The memo states the DA Territory is DE, MD, NJ and PA only (DA §1.12).
The memo is addressed to the Partner and lists issues individually. Each issue gives where it appears (document and section), why it matters, and a recommended fix.
Issues are ordered most significant first, labeled CRITICAL down to LOW. An immediate-actions table identifies what to raise with the client, Velloran and Quillon's counsel.

The memo says a notice sent now is late and not effective under §3.2. The 'protective' notice it suggests is expressly framed as something Velloran will treat as a request for relief, not as a timely renewal.
The memo states that Velloran consent is not listed in Sched. 3.6 and is not covered by §6.4 or §7.1(d).
